div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: A screen or route was checked

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The planner publishes how the product is used, not how it is built
Visible to the worker: route, accessible names, landmarks,
empty, loading and error text, and a test id only where no
user-facing name exists
The worker is free on structure, CSS, files and markup
Hidden with the verifier: the seeded data and the expected results
Tests find things the way a person does. Role and name, not a CSS id
An ARIA snapshot checks the region. A refactor that keeps the
visible behavior keeps passing

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
How the verifier drives it
Screen: Playwright role and label locators, on the attempt
API: HTTP on the attempt's server. Path, method, schemas,
error codes. Schema validation, plus the expected values
Auth: routes, redirects, session properties, failure behavior.
A local mock identity provider covers valid login, bad state,
expired code and wrong role
Job: trigger and observable output, with a fake clock
CLI: command, flags, exit code and output format, in the sandbox
Time rules need an injectable clock. Fake timers at the boundary
instants, in the stated zone. Performance: repeated runs, a
tolerance, a stated dataset size. Concurrency: two clients,
assert the documented outcome

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: What has to be decided next?

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: What failed?

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
After submit, a separate binder sees the inputs and the code,
never the expected values, and writes a small adapter
The adapter may not import expectations or edit product files
The trusted runner compares its observations with the hidden expectations
The entry point is named in the contract before coding.
Red-before-green runs against generated contract stubs, and only
a behavioral failure counts as red. A compile error is a binding bug
If it cannot find an entry point, that is a binding defect
for the author. The brief was underspecified. Not a worker failure
A user-facing entry needs no binder. The runner uses the contract

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Migration, on a fixture at the previous schema
Synthetic edges: nulls, Unicode, max lengths, duplicates,
boundary dates, orphan-looking rows. Tier 3
Assert row counts, checksums of stable columns, each mapping rule,
constraints, indexes, and the app's read path
Run again: it is safe to repeat, or it refuses cleanly
A down-migration round-trips. A slow fixture may shrink,
if the smaller set still covers every rule, and that is recorded
Renames, type changes and drops use expand, then contract:
add new, copy, switch reads, remove old later

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Split the feature
Shell: exact tests with a stub model, including malformed output.
Prompt, parsing, schema, retries, fallbacks, cost limits
Properties: schema, required facts, length, no forbidden content
Quality: a planner eval set of 10 to 30 cases. A judge different
from the generator, a rubric, several samples, a stated threshold
Shown as a score, never a plain green tick
The developer can tighten or loosen the threshold
If the judge is down: verified except quality, and dependents
proceed only if the developer allows
Ordinary CI replays recorded responses. Deterministic, and free

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Contract mismatch. A plain message
It does not count as a hidden-check failure
The contract was already visible to the worker
Renaming Print to Print list is a product revision, not a worker fault
Two buttons with the same name are flagged at planning

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Behavior failure. The hidden-check rules apply
A wrong hidden API, auth, job or CLI result uses this same ladder

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Skip the ladder?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
No more retries at this level
Up one level with the full history, or back to the author
if the brief looks unclear

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Author review. The brief or the expectation is suspect

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: The author decides the dispute

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Which informed attempt is this?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Rule id and text, plus the failure type:
wrong value, missing, extra, wrong order, exception, timeout
The hidden input stays hidden

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A fresh example from the same rule, with expected and actual
The original held-back case stays hidden
A disclosed example joins the visible set. Another stays hidden
Each rule keeps at least three hidden examples
The ladder step lives in verification_state and survives attempts

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Visual layers, from blocking to advice
Structure: ARIA snapshot of landmarks and order. Blocks
Geometry: three widths, no overflow or overlap, within 2 px
of the template, minimum tap size. Blocks
Accessibility: axe-core. Serious issues block
Tokens: no raw colors or arbitrary spacing. Blocks
Pixels: toHaveScreenshot, dynamic regions masked.
Blocks only after an approved baseline
Taste: vision review against the style guide. Advisory

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
External services use that service's test mode or a local emulator
Record how it differs from live. A separately authorized live
check covers what remains
A flaky browser test reruns in a fresh state
A disagreeing run is unstable and goes to its owner

svg.text: Verifying screens, routes, migrations and AI features
